extraction_citation: VERIFIED (2026-07-28) via PubMed structured abstract, PMID 36861092, PMC9969736, doi 10.1093/ofid/ofad051, Open Forum Infect Dis 2023;10(2):ofad051. Screened at the round-3 domain referee's request. 62-year-old woman with a chronic right hip prosthetic joint infection present since 2016. Phage Pa53 given through joint drainage (10 mL q8h on day 1, then 5 mL q8h for 2 weeks) after surgery, with meropenem 2 g q12h IV. Two-year clinical follow-up: no signs of relapse, leukocyte scan clean -> clinical_success_n=1; the abstract's conclusion states phage therapy was 'effective in eradicating infection' -> microbio_eradication_n=1; patient alive -> mortality_n=0. ADVERSE EVENTS DELIBERATELY LEFT NA, NOT ZERO: the source states 'No SEVERE adverse events were observed during PT'. That establishes no severe event; it does not establish an any-adverse-event numerator of zero, and this review's safety outcome is any adverse event. Coding 0 here would silently mix a severe-AE denominator into an any-AE pool -- the exact defect the round-3 domain referee identified. RESISTANCE NOT CLASSIFIABLE: the abstract reports no susceptibility panel and applies no MDR/XDR/PDR label.
incomplete_reason: Abstract-only extraction. adverse_event_n left NA because only severe AEs are reported (see citation). Resistance not classifiable. Full text (PMC9969736) available but not consulted in this pass.

clinical_success_definition: Extensive chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa osteoarticular infection in a 7-year-old: a significant therapeutic effect was documented within two weeks of starting adjunctive phage therapy, averting the catastrophic outcome the therapy was attempted to avoid
extraction_citation: VERIFIED (2026-07-28) via PubMed structured abstract, PMID 34369652, PMC8422068, doi 10.15252/emmm.202113936, EMBO Mol Med 2021;13(9):e13936. Screened at the round-3 domain referee's request; MeSH confirms Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Phage Therapy. Seven-year-old child with extensive chronic P. aeruginosa osteoarticular infection, adjunctive phage therapy with real-time dose adjustment from phage and bacterial kinetics. 'A significant therapeutic effect within two weeks' -> clinical_success_n=1. Patient alive -> mortality_n=0. Eradication not reported -> NA. ADVERSE EVENT POSITIVE: the abstract reports 'transient fever and local pain' associated with early bacterial-lysis release, with marked upregulation of innate-immunity genes -> adverse_event_n=1, coded harm-conservatively as a treatment-associated event even though the authors frame it mechanistically rather than as toxicity. ROUTE NOT REPORTED: the abstract does not state the administration route and this review does not infer it; coded 'not reported' so the arm sits in the same NA-route category as Malhotra 2026 and Arya 2026 rather than being guessed into a stratum. RESISTANCE NOT CLASSIFIABLE: no susceptibility panel and no MDR/XDR/PDR label in the abstract.
incomplete_reason: Abstract-only extraction. Route and eradication not reported; resistance not classifiable. Full text (PMC8422068) available but not consulted in this pass.
